doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: The booker and the barn gig in the South
summary: Woody's booker skimmed money and booked the band into a barn for $400-500.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Exactly. And one funny thing is when we were on the road, Abe Turchin — I think that was his name — he was the booker for Woody. And he was actually siphoning money from Woody and Woody didn’t realize it. But he booked us in a barn someplace in the south. I’m not sure whether it was in Arkansas, Alabama, someplace. But we were in the hills. And it was a big barn. People came in with coveralls and women with long dresses and wide dresses, and we are playing jazz, and then we’d play dance music too for them. There might have been maybe 100 people, 125 people there. But he booked that just for transportation. I think Woody made $500 for that night, maybe $400.
Yeah. For the whole band for a four hour job. But that’s when I was still riding in cars with the other guys.
